title: He rode a donkey… once.
paragraphs:
Because the same Jesus people ignore today…
is the King they won’t escape tomorrow.
You’ve heard of Him as Savior.

The One who eats with sinners.
The One who touches the unclean.
The One who says, “Come to Me.” (Matthew 11:28)
But Revelation 19 doesn’t show Him reaching out…
And most people aren’t ready for that version of Jesus.

We love a Jesus who forgives…
but we resist a Jesus who rules.

We want grace without surrender.
Mercy without repentance.
Salvation without transformation.

We say we follow Him—
but our pride still sits on the throne.

We sing worship songs—
but our secret sin still has a private room.

We post verses—
but our hearts haven’t bowed.
We think we still have time.
But here’s the tension you can’t ignore:

What if the Jesus you keep delaying…
is already standing at the edge of eternity?
What if mercy has an expiration date?

What if the next time heaven opens…
it’s not for salvation—but for judgment?
“And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse! The one sitting on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war.” (Revelation 19:11)
“His eyes are like a flame of fire… and on His head are many diadems.” (Revelation 19:12)

Every secret thought.
Every private compromise.
Every moment you said, “It’s not that serious.”
“From His mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations…” (Revelation 19:15)

The same Word you ignored.
The same truth you scrolled past.
The same conviction you silenced.
Now becomes the standard that judges.
“He will tread the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty.” (Revelation 19:15)
Sin is not cute to God.

It’s not “just a phase.”
It’s not “who I am.”
Is the same One who took it.

Before Revelation 19…
there was a cross.

Before the white horse…
there was a wooden beam.

Before the crown of many diadems…
there was a crown of thorns.
“But He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities…” (Isaiah 53:5)
Jesus didn’t just come to warn you about judgment.
You are not judged because God hates you.
You are judged because sin is real.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
While you were still in it.

Still hiding.
Still pretending.
Still delaying.

Covered by His blood.
Forgiven. Restored. Free.
Because you don’t get both versions at the same time.

Some scholars interpret Revelation 19 as both a literal future event and a symbolic unveiling of Christ’s ultimate authority over all evil. But whether you read it symbolically or literally, the truth remains unshaken:
So let me ask you—no filters, no pretending:
What are you still holding onto?

That secret habit?
That pride you won’t release?
That delayed obedience?
This is not a message to crush you.
This is a call to wake you.
Because the same King who rides in judgment…
“Seek the Lord while He may be found; call upon Him while He is near.” (Isaiah 55:6)
Trust in Jesus—not your effort, not your morality, not your image.
Revelation 19 is no longer your fear.
Because the King you see riding…
